data.text:
# M3 C2 lookup memory accounting

Collected 2026-11-16 from the current frozen C2 headers and
`tools/lookup_memory_probe.cpp`. This is allocation/capacity accounting only;
it contains no throughput or latency measurement.

## Method

- Built the standalone probe and a small `sizeof`/`alignof` harness with the
  Makefile-probed control compiler (`/usr/bin/clang++`, Clang 23.1.4),
  `PERF_MODE=control`, and the flags captured by `make -s
  PERF_MODE=control perf-print-flags`. No PGO flags or engine objects were
  used. The exact control CXXFLAGS are recorded in `abi.json`.
- Ran the probe serially with requested sizes 10,000, 100,000, and 1,000,000.
  Raw CSV output is in `count-10000.csv`, `count-100000.csv`, and
  `count-1000000.csv`.
- The probe reports current and peak bytes requested through its PMR resource.
  Its own pointer ledger uses the default allocator, outside that resource.
  `std::unordered_map` columns are allocation controls measured through the
  same counting resource; reserved controls call `reserve(live_count)` first.
  These are allocator-requested bytes/capacities, not process RSS or complete
  object footprint. Timing was not collected.
- In `byRef` rows, the CSV field named
  `overflow_or_mapped_value_bytes` is actually the `FlatU32Map` bucket
  capacity (a slot count), not a byte count. In `births-prepared` rows the
  corresponding field is the mapped-value size in bytes. The PMR
  `current_bytes` and `peak_bytes` fields are byte counts for both.

## C2 known-short versus an intentionally inflated known hint

Both rows below are current C2 measurements with different *provided known*
hints. The three-entry fixture uses keys 1, 5,000, and 9,999. With its known
path count of 148, `byRef` has dense capacity 64 values plus 8 presence bytes;
its sparse overflow has bucket capacity 8. At the measured 48-byte pair size
plus one presence bit per bucket, that overflow contributes 66 bytes. The
measured current and peak PMR bytes are both 330 (256 value bytes + 8
presence bytes + 66 overflow bytes). Birth-map current/peak is 272 bytes. The
same fixture with an intentionally inflated known 10,000-op hint produces
`byRef` dense capacity 10,000, 1,250
presence bytes, no overflow allocation, current 41,250 bytes, and peak 61,875
bytes. Birth-map bytes are unchanged at 272.

The 10,000-op-hint row is an accounting proxy for an inflated known hint; it
is not the unknown-hint fallback (which uses 4,096) and is not a historical C1
production measurement. Both fixture rows repeat identically in all three
requested-size runs because the fixture remains three entries and varies only
its hint. They demonstrate capacity effects, not a speed benefit.

## ABI sizes

The standalone C2 header harness reports `Manifold` 488 bytes (alignment 8),
`ManifoldOpIndexMap` 216 bytes (alignment 8), and
`StructureBirthInfo` 40 bytes (alignment 8). A
`pair<const uint32_t, StructureBirthInfo>` is 48 bytes. The `std::unordered_map`
and `std::pmr::unordered_map` container headers are 56 and 64 bytes,
respectively. These header/object sizes are separate from dynamic PMR bytes and
are not shared-memory totals.

The archived comparison artifact
[m3-abi-accounting.json](/data/git/gleditor-restore/build/performance/comparisons/m3-abi-accounting.json)
has SHA-256
`59837afb4354a78c09fd8624344858962b5bdfe8a9a35480bc3fa74245dae58e`.
It records P3 at 296 bytes and the prior C hybrid-unordered variant at 544
bytes. Against those archived measurements, current C2 at 488 bytes is +192
bytes versus P3 and 56 bytes below prior C. These comparisons use the
artifact's recorded compiler/stdlib/flags and are header-size differences
only. The full current C2 source hashes, compiler target, standard library,
and build flags are in `abi.json`.
